# Using Maestro in Codex

<!-- Generated by `node packages/cli build` from the harness registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

The skill is the same in every agent. This guide covers only what is specific to Codex.

## Install

Project scope (one repository): copy this skill folder to `.agents/skills/maestro/`.

User scope (every project): copy it to `~/.agents/skills/maestro/`.

From the gti-skills repository, the CLI does the copy for you:

```bash
node packages/cli install --harness codex --skill maestro
node packages/cli install --harness codex --skill maestro --scope user
```

Restart the agent session after installing so it rescans its skills.

## Use

Describe the task in plain language. Codex loads the skill when the request matches its `description`. You can also name it in the request, for example: "Use the maestro skill to ...".

## Where the skill finds its files

`<skill-dir>` in `SKILL.md` is the folder that contains `SKILL.md`: `.agents/skills/maestro` for a project install, or `~/.agents/skills/maestro` for a user install. Scripts and references are always addressed relative to it.

## Verify

Ask the agent which skills it has loaded and check that `maestro` is listed.

## Notes

- Scan paths come from community guides; /etc/codex/skills is the admin location. Codex configuration lives in ~/.codex.
- Maestro delegates every step. Load the model preferences and the provider catalog before choosing a worker. Paseo can drive Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Cline, Cursor, Kilo, Hermes, Antigravity, Muse, and ACP providers. Read references/harness/adapters.md before the first spawn, and record the worker chat id before the first prompt.
- Codex records a session id in codex exec --json output and resumes it with codex exec resume <session-id>.
- Documentation: [Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills) (path source: community).
